note: The attacker-controlled config file line 'enum fruit 5' is read from the file and parsed into token='enum' and cptr='fruit 5'.
The 'enum' token handler (se_read_conf) was registered by init_snmp_enum, so run_config_handler dispatches to se_read_conf with cptr='fruit 5'.
First word 'fruit' is copied into e_name; sscanf(e_name, "%d:%d", &major, &minor) returns 0, so the named-enumeration branch is taken.
Next word '5' is copied into the stack buffer e_enum as the string "5\0".
sscanf("5", "%d:", &value) returns 1 because %d matches '5' and the literal ':' is not required to match, so the loop body is entered.
cp2 points at e_enum="5\0". The loop reads '5', then '\0', then continues reading past the end of the 8192-byte e_enum stack buffer looking for a ':', causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
